# get_kmeans_init { #dyf.get_kmeans_init }

```python
get_kmeans_init(
    embeddings,
    nlist,
    use_stable_bridges=True,
    num_stability_seeds=5,
    stability_threshold=3,
    global_num_bits=12,
    seed=42,
    verbose=False,
)
```

Get bridge-seeded initial centroids for k-means/IVF index construction.

Using orthogonal bridge points as k-means initialization provides:
- +1% recall improvement over standard k-means++
- 17-24% fewer bucket probes needed for same recall
- Better bucket coherence (neighbors land in same bucket more often)

The returned centroids can be used with sklearn.cluster.KMeans or FAISS IVF.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name                | Type                                     | Description                                                   | Default    |
|---------------------|------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| embeddings          | [np](`numpy`).[ndarray](`numpy.ndarray`) | Normalized embeddings (n, d)                                  | _required_ |
| nlist               | [int](`int`)                             | Number of clusters/centroids (IVF nlist parameter)            | _required_ |
| use_stable_bridges  | [bool](`bool`)                           | If True, prefer bridges stable across multiple seeds          | `True`     |
| num_stability_seeds | [int](`int`)                             | Number of seeds for stability testing                         | `5`        |
| stability_threshold | [int](`int`)                             | Minimum seeds a bridge must appear in (if use_stable_bridges) | `3`        |
| global_num_bits     | [int](`int`)                             | LSH bits for bridge detection                                 | `12`       |
| seed                | [int](`int`)                             | Random seed                                                   | `42`       |
| verbose             | [bool](`bool`)                           | Print progress                                                | `False`    |

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                     | Description                                                            |
|--------|------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [np](`numpy`).[ndarray](`numpy.ndarray`) | Initial centroids array (nlist, d) suitable for k-means init parameter |

## Example {.doc-section .doc-section-example}

>>> from dyf import get_kmeans_init
>>> from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
>>>
>>> # Get bridge-seeded initialization
>>> init = get_kmeans_init(embeddings, nlist=1000)
>>>
>>> # Use with sklearn
>>> kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=1000, init=init, n_init=1)
>>> kmeans.fit(embeddings)
>>>
>>> # Use with FAISS
>>> import faiss
>>> quantizer = faiss.IndexFlatIP(dim)
>>> quantizer.add(kmeans.cluster_centers_)

## Note {.doc-section .doc-section-note}

For high-recall requirements (99%+), consider using
`candidate_indices=np.arange(len(embeddings))` in select_orthogonal_anchors
instead, as all-points expansion provides better long-tail coverage.
